# IPTVMac

> IPTVMac is a free, open source IPTV player for Mac, Windows, iPhone and iPad, Android phones and tablets, and Android TV, Google TV and Fire TV. It plays Xtream Codes and M3U sources with a built-in mpv player, instant search, subtitles, Picture in Picture, catch-up, downloads and an interface in 31 languages. Mac: Apple Silicon, macOS 14 or later. Android: 8 or later (APK on GitHub Releases, including TV files). GPL-3.0. It is a player only and includes no channels or content.

Latest version: 0.9.8. Download: https://github.com/Goelir/IPTVMac/releases/latest
Install in Terminal: `curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Goelir/IPTVMac/main/install.sh | bash`
Install video (95 seconds, English): https://youtu.be/TgaoFEEMg48
Source code: https://github.com/Goelir/IPTVMac
Privacy policy: https://goelir.github.io/IPTVMac/privacy/ (no account, no analytics, no ads, no tracking; nothing is sent to the developer)
iPhone and iPad app (completely free: no ads, no subscription, no in-app purchases; iOS 17 or later): https://apps.apple.com/app/id6821761790
Downloads (Mac, Windows, Android, Android TV, iPhone and iPad): https://goelir.github.io/IPTVMac/download/
Platform pages: Mac https://goelir.github.io/IPTVMac/mac/ , Windows https://goelir.github.io/IPTVMac/windows/ , iPhone and iPad https://goelir.github.io/IPTVMac/iphone/ , Android https://goelir.github.io/IPTVMac/android/ , Android TV / Google TV / Fire TV https://goelir.github.io/IPTVMac/tv/
Features: https://goelir.github.io/IPTVMac/features/
Release notes: https://goelir.github.io/IPTVMac/changelog/
Support: https://goelir.github.io/IPTVMac/support/ (how to add a source, troubleshooting, how to report a bug without sharing a login)

## Guides
- [How to watch Xtream Codes IPTV on a Mac](https://goelir.github.io/IPTVMac/guides/xtream-codes-on-mac.html): Install IPTVMac, choose Xtream Codes, and enter the server address, username and password your provider gave you. IPTVMac downloads the channel list once and then searches it instantly.
- [How to play an M3U playlist on a Mac](https://goelir.github.io/IPTVMac/guides/m3u-playlist-on-mac.html): Install IPTVMac, choose M3U, and enter a name and the playlist link. IPTVMac reads the playlist and sorts it into Live, Movies and Series.
- [Picture in Picture for IPTV on a Mac](https://goelir.github.io/IPTVMac/guides/picture-in-picture-iptv-mac.html): Start any channel or movie in IPTVMac and click the Picture in Picture button in the player. The video moves to a small floating window that stays on top of other apps and across Spaces.
- [How to add Xtream Codes IPTV on a Fire TV](https://goelir.github.io/IPTVMac/guides/xtream-codes-on-fire-tv.html): Install the Downloader app on the TV, use it to install IPTVMac, then open IPTVMac and enter the server address, username and password from your provider.
- [How to play an M3U playlist on iPhone and iPad](https://goelir.github.io/IPTVMac/guides/m3u-playlist-on-iphone.html): Install IPTVMac from the App Store, choose M3U, give the source a name and paste the playlist link. The app sorts it into Live, Movies and Series.
- [How to watch IPTV on Windows 10 and 11](https://goelir.github.io/IPTVMac/guides/iptv-player-windows.html): Download the IPTVMac installer, run it (no administrator rights needed), and add your Xtream Codes login or M3U link.
- [How to set up IPTV on an Android phone](https://goelir.github.io/IPTVMac/guides/iptv-on-android.html): Download the arm64-v8a APK, open it and allow the install, then add your Xtream Codes login or M3U link in IPTVMac.
- [How to watch past programs (catch-up) on a Mac](https://goelir.github.io/IPTVMac/guides/catch-up-iptv-mac.html): Play a live channel that supports catch-up, click Watch from the past in the player, and pick a program from the guide. Your provider must keep an archive for that channel.
- [IPTV keeps buffering? What to check](https://goelir.github.io/IPTVMac/guides/iptv-buffering.html): Most buffering comes from the provider or the network, not the player. Close other players that use the same login, try a wired connection, compare a few channels, and on the Mac raise the network buffer in Settings.

## Facts
- Requirements: Apple Silicon Mac (M1 or later), macOS 14 or later. Intel Macs are not supported.
- Free playlists: the independent project iptv-org (github.com/iptv-org/iptv) publishes M3U playlists of publicly available channels, e.g. https://iptv-org.github.io/iptv/index.m3u ; IPTVMac is not affiliated with it.
- Sources: Xtream Codes (server address, username, password) and M3U (playlist link). A local .m3u file is not supported yet.
- Player: mpv (libmpv, bundled). Hardware decoding, automatic reconnect, embedded and external subtitles, playback speed from 0.25x to 4x for movies and episodes, configurable skip step, fit/fill/stretch, sleep timer.
- Several playlists: switch between them or show all playlists together (search, favorites and continue watching across all).
- Settings: light/dark appearance, interface language, automatic playlist refresh, hiding categories by words, backup and restore (playlists without passwords, favorites, history).
- Search: local SQLite full-text search, inside a category, inside a section or everywhere.
- Picture in Picture: IPTVMac's own always-on-top floating window, across Spaces.
- Catch-up and program guide on channels whose provider supports them (Xtream).
- Downloads of movies and episodes (whole seasons on Xtream series) to a folder the user chooses.
- Next episode starts automatically after a 5 second countdown (can be turned off).
- Free, no ads, no tracking. Passwords are stored in the app's local database, readable only by the user.
- Signing: from version 0.9.1, releases are signed with an Apple Developer ID and notarized by Apple (an automated malware scan, not a review of the app), so the DMG opens with a normal double-click. Versions before 0.9.1 are not notarized: install them with the Terminal command above (it works for every version), or choose Open Anyway in System Settings, Privacy and Security.

## FAQ
- What is IPTVMac? IPTVMac is a free, open source IPTV player for Mac, Android phones and tablets, and Android TV, Google TV and Fire TV (and an iPhone and iPad app on the App Store). It plays Xtream Codes and M3U sources with a built-in mpv player, instant search, subtitles, Picture in Picture, catch-up, downloads and an interface in 31 languages.
- Does IPTVMac include channels or a subscription? No. IPTVMac is only a player. It does not include or host any channels, movies or series. You add a source from a provider you are authorized to use. If you have none, the independent open source project iptv-org publishes free playlists of publicly available channels; see the link on this page.
- Does it work with Xtream Codes and M3U? Yes. For Xtream Codes you enter the server address, username and password from your provider. For M3U you enter a name and the playlist link.
- Which Macs are supported? Apple Silicon Macs (M1 or later) with macOS 14 or later. Intel Macs are not supported.
- Is there an iPhone, iPad or Android version? Android: yes. Download the APK from GitHub Releases (https://github.com/Goelir/IPTVMac/releases/tag/android-v1.0.7); it has a touch player, Picture in Picture, sound with the screen off and downloads for offline viewing, and needs Android 8 or later. Android TV, Google TV and Fire TV: the same release has a 32-bit and a 64-bit file for TVs (remote-control friendly, no downloads on TV, first version, installed directly with the Downloader app or from a USB stick; there is no store listing yet). iPhone and iPad: yes, the app is on the App Store (https://apps.apple.com/app/id6821761790) and it is completely free: no ads, no subscription, no in-app purchases. It needs iOS 17 or later and has the same 31 languages and the same no-account, no-tracking design. All share the engine, the 31 languages and the no-account, no-tracking design of the Mac app, and the source is in the same GitHub repository.
- Is the App Store version different from the one on GitHub? It is the same iPhone and iPad app and the same code. The App Store version installs with one tap and updates itself after Apple has reviewed each version; GitHub is usually a little ahead. If you build it from GitHub yourself you sign it with your own Apple ID (a free account lasts 7 days, a paid one a year) and update by building again. Mac, Windows and Android are not in an app store: the files on GitHub are the only versions.
- Is IPTVMac free? Yes. It is free and open source under the GPL-3.0 license, with no ads and no tracking.
- Why does macOS block the app, and how do I open it? Versions before 0.9.1 are not notarized by Apple, so macOS blocks a copy that was downloaded in a browser. From version 0.9.1, releases are signed with an Apple Developer ID and notarized, and the DMG opens with a normal double-click. To fix an older copy, install the latest release (the DMG, or the one-line command above, which works for every version), or open System Settings, Privacy and Security, and choose Open Anyway.
- Does IPTVMac have Picture in Picture? Yes. A floating window stays on top of other apps and across Spaces while you browse for something else.
- Can I watch past programs (catch-up)? Yes, on channels where your provider supports catch-up. Pick a program from the guide.
- Is it safe to use? The source code is public. Updates come from GitHub Releases and are checked against a SHA-256 checksum. Account passwords are stored in the app's local database, readable only by your user.

## Not to be confused with
IPTVMac is not an IPTV provider and does not sell subscriptions or channels.
